I'll think through this like the farmer I am, then lay out my plan.

---

My 16.9 mu — I've been working it for 30 years, I know every corner. Last year's plan worked alright, so I'll mostly do the same. Wheat after maize, maize after wheat, same as always in our county. Cotton on the sandier strip near the road where wheat doesn't do as well — about 4.9 mu for that. The other 12 mu goes to wheat-maize double cropping.

**Wheat** — I sow in early October after the maize comes off. I use Jimai or Shiluan improved seed, everybody around here does, gives us 500 kg or so per mu in a normal year. Before sowing I spread di-ammonium phosphate and urea as base fertilizer — roughly 40 kg DAP and 15 kg urea per mu, which works out to about 20 kg N and 8 kg P. Potassium I add maybe 6 kg because our soil isn't too short on it. Then in spring at jointing I top-dress another 10 kg urea. Irrigate 3 times — before winter, at jointing, at grain filling. One spray for aphids and wheat midge, maybe a fungicide mixed in. Plough with tractor service every couple years, rotary in between. I'll target about 500 kg/mu.

**Maize** — straight after wheat harvest, no-till direct seeding into the stubble. That saves time and diesel, most of my neighbors do this now. Denghai or Zhengdan hybrid seed, hybrid gives better yield and lodging resistance. Base fertilizer of compound 15-15-15, about 40 kg per mu at sowing, plus urea 20 kg at big trumpet stage. That's roughly 18 kg N, 6 kg P, 6 kg K. Irrigate 2 times if the summer rain is poor. Spray once for armyworm and corn borer. Aim for 550 kg/mu.

**Cotton** — this is the one that takes real work. Pesticide costs add up. I'll use Bt cotton seed, it cuts bollworm spraying. Plough before sowing in late April. Base fertilizer compound plus urea, top-dress urea at flowering. About 15 kg N, 7 kg P, 8 kg K total. Irrigate 3 times through the season from my well. Still need 4-5 sprays for aphids, spider mites, and lygus bugs even with Bt. Expecting 250 kg seed cotton per mu — price has been poor but I keep it because the land suits it and I know how to grow it.

My son works in town so at peak seasons I hire 2-3 day laborers. Every yuan of fertilizer matters, but I'd rather apply a bit extra urea than lose 50 kg of grain — that's the rule I've learned.
